section 5.1.2, which states the formula for least squares

Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman (2009), ESL 2e, section 7.10.1,
states the same identity for linear fitting methods.

:::{#thm-loocv-shortcut}
#### Leave-one-out cross-validation for least squares

For a linear model fitted by [ordinary least squares](correlation-regression.qmd#def-ols)
with every [leverage](#def-leverage) $\lev{i} < 1$,
the [leave-one-out estimate](#def-loocv)
can be computed from the single fit to all $n$ observations,
from its [prediction errors](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-error)
$\prederr_i = \fitted_i - y_i$ and its leverages:

$$
\cvest{n} = \frac{1}{n} \sumin \sqf{\frac{\prederr_i}{1 - \lev{i}}}.
$$ {#eq-loocv-shortcut}

:::

::: proof
We state this without proof;
see @james2021islr2e [sec. 5.1.2]
and @hastie2009elements [sec. 7.10.1].
@exm-loocv-shortcut checks it numerically.
:::
